lines.cap: Their leader got young men so high, they'd jump off a castle wall for him. At least, that's what his enemies said.
lines.say: Their leader got young men so high, they'd jump off a castle wall for him. At least, that's what his enemies said.

lines.cap: The Nizari Ismailis. Persia and Syria, from 1090. A small group, surrounded by huge empires. So they fought a different way.
lines.say: The Nizari Ismailis. Persia and Syria, from 1090. A small group, surrounded by huge empires. So they fought a different way.

lines.cap: Their leader, Hasan-i Sabbah, took a mountain fortress called Alamut. And never left it again. Reportedly, for over thirty years.
lines.say: Their leader, Hasan-i Sabbah, took a mountain fortress called Alamut. And never left it again. Reportedly, for over thirty years.

lines.cap: Instead of armies, they sent single agents. Trained for years, to get close to a powerful target. A sultan. A general. A vizier.
lines.say: Instead of armies, they sent single agents. Trained for years, to get close to a powerful target. A sultan. A general. A vizier.

lines.cap: Often in public. Often with a dagger. And often they didn't try to escape.
lines.say: Often in public. Often with a dagger. And often they didn't try to escape.

lines.cap: Their enemies called them hashishiyya. Hashish users. Marco Polo told of a secret garden and drugged recruits. Historians say there's no real evidence.
lines.say: Their enemies called them hashishiyya. Hashish users. Marco Polo told of a secret garden and drugged recruits. Historians say there's no real evidence.

lines.cap: But the nickname stuck. In English, it became a word. Assassin.
lines.say: But the nickname stuck. In English, it became a word. Assassin.
